Purpose

The internal state tracker, _next_stored_block_idx, was being updated prematurely. The code would advance this index immediately after a successful prepare_store call, but before the actual offload operation was queued.

If any condition caused the code to exit before the operation was added to the reqs_to_store queue, the scheduler's state would become inconsistent. It would believe the blocks had been handled for offloading when, in fact, they had been skipped. This resulted in those blocks never being offloaded, effectively causing data loss from the cache.

The update to _next_stored_block_idx is moved to occur only after the offload operation has been successfully added to the queue.

Specifically:

  1. If all blocks are already cached (no new blocks to store), the index is updated, as the state is confirmed.
  2. If new blocks need to be stored, the index is now updated only after the transfer specification is successfully created and added to reqs_to_store.

Code Review

This pull request addresses a race condition in the KV cache offloading mechanism where the internal state tracker _next_stored_block_idx was updated prematurely, before the offload operation was actually queued. This could lead to an inconsistent state and potential data loss from the cache. The fix correctly defers the update of _next_stored_block_idx until after the offload operation has been successfully queued, or when it's confirmed that all blocks are already cached and no offload is needed. The changes are logical, well-targeted, and effectively resolve the described race condition, making the code more robust. I have reviewed the changes and found no issues.

orozery commented Oct 29, 2025

Copy link
Copy Markdown
Collaborator

@albertoperdomo2 this PR basically groups the two updates together:

self._reqs_being_stored[req_id] |= block_hashes_to_store
self._next_stored_block_idx[req_id] = num_blocks

Previously, these updates where separated by a few lines.
I don't see any possible error path in those lines that could yield a case where only the first operation (writing to _next_stored_block_idx) is performed.
Also, the scheduler is single-threaded, so I would not call it a race condition.

Nevertheless, I'm good with this change.
Just want to verify my understanding that this is not a current bug, but rather proofing against possible future bugs.
Correct?
